How much of the gallery is covered?

Loading snapshot details…

This is a saved snapshot. Links and offers can change after capture.

What can I trust about availability?

“Store link listed” means a URL is present, not that the app is released, compatible, free, or installable. Web links may lead to landing pages. “Demo mentioned” is a developer statement. Unknown stays unknown.

How are projects selected and ordered?

The default order shows matching Featured projects first, followed by a stable shuffle seeded by the snapshot date. FingerSling and ClayBox Touch are editorially featured in Play & puzzle and Create & design respectively. Search and access filters still apply, and choosing Name A–Z or Most public likes uses that order. Surprise me gives matching Featured projects an extra chance: one in five draws uses the Featured pool when one is available; the other draws use all matching projects. Featured placement is separate from measured analytics and judging results. Guided collections use keyword rules and these editorial inclusions, published with the code. Projects can appear in multiple collections. “One like or fewer” describes exposure, not quality.

Where does my shortlist live?

Saved project IDs stay in your browser’s local storage. No account is required. Clearing browser storage removes them, and they don’t automatically sync across devices. Shared shortlist links contain only the selected public project IDs.

Found a mistake?

Suggest a correction on GitHub. Include the Devpost project URL, the field, and a public source supporting the change. Corrections are reviewed before appearing here.

READING THE SIGNALS

A label you can question.

Confidence describes the source of a claim. It does not grade the project.

Observed
Directly present on a captured public page: a link, image, team listing, or embedded video. A listed link is not a tested app.
Developer-reported
A statement or technology tag supplied by the developer. Availability and feature claims have not been independently verified.
Estimated
A keyword rule suggests a category, theme, or collection. You can inspect the explanation and source.
Unknown
The inspected sources don’t establish the answer. Missing information is not treated as “no.”
